# Refusals and how to recover

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen_skill_reference.py from src/milkshake/errors.py: do not edit by hand. Add a typed error with a `default_alternative` and run `mise run skill:reference`; tests/skill/ fails when this drifts or lacks a code. -->

178 typed failures. Every one is a `MilkshakeError` with a stable code, and with `--json` it prints `{"ok": false, "error": {"code", "message", "alternative"}}`, plus `"next_command"` when one `ms` command resolves it (never for integrity failures). The exit code says how bad: 3 refused (nothing was written), 4 blocked (a gate; the items are listed), 5 integrity or an external write whose outcome is unknown. The `message` of a real run names the specifics (ids, amounts, the clause); the recovery below is the generic remedy the error's `alternative` carries.

The **who** column says whose move it is:

- `you`: fix the cause with the recovery and re-run the same command.
- `operator`: tell an operator and stop; the fix is a decision (a grant, a contract term, a credential, an override) and never yours to make or to work around.
- `stop`: integrity. Stop writing, do not repair anything, tell an operator.

The `FARM_*` command refusals (`FARM_MODE_FORBIDDEN` and the like) have no CLI exit: they appear on `farm.command.handled` and `farm.command.ran` events and the Farm's `commands` list. The `FARM_RUN_*` codes are statuses of a palette run, never raised.

| code | exit | who | what happened | recovery |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ACCEPT_INCOMPLETE_REFUSED` | 3 | operator | `--accept-incomplete` was refused: a blocking client-borne scope is material. | Make the scope an actual (squeeze after the period closes, or record the vendor's own invoice with `ms boi add --manual`). The override covers only an immaterial residual: at most the smaller of USD 1.00 or 1% of the total. |
| `ACTOR_UNRESOLVED` | 3 | you | Actor unresolved. | Set MILKSHAKE_ACTOR (agents use e.g. milkshake-pm@agents.automaticai.io) or git config user.email, then retry. |
| `ADJUST_AMOUNT_FORBIDDEN` | 3 | you | Adjust amount forbidden. | Vendor amounts are immutable: a correction is a new revision recorded with `ms boi add --manual ... --reference ... --evidence-file ...`. `ms adjust item` changes only who bears the cost (--bill-to, --split-cap/--split-bps) or the markup (--margin, --margin-bps). |
| `ADJUST_EMPTY` | 3 | you | Adjust empty. | Pass at least one of --bill-to, --split-cap, --split-bps, --margin, --margin-bps. |
| `AR_AMOUNT_INVALID` | 3 | you | Ar amount invalid. | Mercury invoices need a positive total and a due date; see ms yrd show. |
| `AR_CANCEL_NOT_ALLOWED` | 3 | operator | Ar cancel not allowed. | Only an Unpaid AR invoice can be cancelled; use MILKSHAKE_AR_SUPERSEDE=delta. |
| `AR_DELTA_INVALID` | 3 | operator | Ar delta invalid. | A delta invoice needs a revised total above what Mercury AR already bills. |
| `AR_DESTINATION_AMBIGUOUS` | 3 | operator | Ar destination ambiguous. | Keep exactly one active checking account in Mercury (archive the other), then retry: the invoice instructs the client to pay into it. |
| `AR_DESTINATION_MISSING` | 3 | operator | Ar destination missing. | Open a checking account in Mercury to receive the payment, then retry. |
| `AR_NUMBER_EXISTS` | 3 | operator | Ar number exists. | A Mercury AR number is never reused; reconcile the existing invoice. |
| `AR_SUPERSEDE_REFUSED` | 3 | operator | Ar supersede refused. | Set MILKSHAKE_AR_SUPERSEDE=cancel_recreate or delta (Q14), or send the revised statement without a Mercury invoice. |
| `AUDIT_FINDING_AMBIGUOUS` | 3 | you | The finding id prefix matches more than one finding. | Give more characters of the id (the full F-xxxxxxxx form). |
| `AUDIT_FINDING_UNKNOWN` | 3 | you | `ms audit feedback` named a finding no recorded run (or a re-derived audit) contains. | Use the id an `ms audit` run printed (F-xxxxxxxx). Findings of a plain run are found again with --client and --period; a model finding needs a recorded run (`ms audit --llm` records one, or add --record). |
| `AUDIT_LLM_REJECTED` | 3 | operator | The gateway refused the audit's token or model (401, 403, 404, 429). | Check the token is the milkshake-audit consumer token, still unexpired (`ops/gateway-tokens.py status milkshake-audit`) and scoped to the model (MILKSHAKE_AUDIT_LLM_MODEL, default automaticai/mistral-allowance/mistral-small). |
| `AUDIT_LLM_REPLY_INVALID` | 3 | you | The model's reply held no usable findings JSON. | Re-run `ms audit --llm`; the deterministic findings stand without it (nothing was recorded). |
| `AUDIT_LLM_TOKEN_INVALID` | 3 | operator | The audit's gateway token is not usable: empty, an unresolved `op://` reference, the value of another loaded credential, or not a plain bearer token (NFR-10). | Mint a dedicated consumer token for milkshake-audit on the gateway (ops/gateway-tokens.py mint) and reference it in .env.vendors.op as MILKSHAKE_AUDIT_LLM_TOKEN; never reuse a vendor, client or management key. |
| `AUDIT_LLM_UNAVAILABLE` | 3 | you | The model pass could not complete: the gateway was unreachable or answered with an error. The deterministic findings are unaffected (re-run without --llm). | Re-run later, or run without --llm for the deterministic audit (nothing was recorded). |
| `AUDIT_LLM_UNCONFIGURED` | 3 | operator | `ms audit --llm` without a gateway token for the model pass (NFR-10). | Run it through `mise run ms -- audit --llm ...` so op run injects MILKSHAKE_AUDIT_LLM_TOKEN from .env.vendors.op (a per-consumer gateway token for Milkshake), or drop --llm: the deterministic audit needs no model and works offline. |
| `BACKUP_MISMATCH` | 5 | stop | Backup mismatch. | Retry the backup; the copy did not contain the source head. |
| `BACKUP_TARGET_EXISTS` | 3 | you | Backup target exists. | Choose a new backup path; backups never overwrite an existing file. |
| `BOI_ID_AMBIGUOUS` | 3 | you | Boi id ambiguous. | Give more characters of the boi id until it is unique. |
| `BOI_ID_TOO_SHORT` | 3 | you | Boi id too short. | Give at least 8 hex characters of the boi id. |
| `BOI_IS_HISTORY` | 3 | you | Boi is history. | An imported legacy reading is history: it is never billed, so there is nothing to adjust. Read it with `ms boi show`; to bill the month, record the vendor's figure with `ms boi add --manual ... --reference ... --evidence-file ...` or squeeze it. |
| `BOI_NOT_EFFECTIVE` | 3 | you | Boi not effective. | Adjust the scope's effective boi instead: `ms boi list --client C --period YYYY-MM` shows it (a newer revision or a manual entry replaced this one). |
| `BOI_UNKNOWN` | 3 | you | Boi unknown. | Find ids with `ms boi list --client C --period YYYY-MM --json`. |
| `BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE` | 3 | operator | The browser capability (Kapture, `MILKSHAKE_KAPTURE_URL`) could not be reached or could not drive the vendor's page (no server, not signed in, the page changed). | `BUS_NOT_CONFIGURED` | 3 | operator | Publishing to Bloodbank needs `MILKSHAKE_NATS_URL` and the `bus` extra. | Set MILKSHAKE_NATS_URL (nats://127.0.0.1:4222 on big-chungus) and install the bus extra (`mise run tool:install`). Nothing was published; the ledger is unaffected. |
| `BUS_UNAVAILABLE` | 3 | operator | Bloodbank could not be reached or did not confirm a publish. The ledger is unaffected. | Retry later. Publishing is idempotent (the event id is derived from the ledger event hash), and the outbox republishes anything unconfirmed on its own. |

| `CATEGORY_NAMER_UNCONFIGURED` | 3 | you | `ms category propose --apply` has groups to name and no gateway token (Story 9.4). | Run it through `mise run ms -- category propose --apply` so op run injects MILKSHAKE_CATEGORY_LLM_TOKEN (a per-consumer AutomaticAI gateway token for Milkshake). | `CATEGORY_TOO_MANY` | 3 | operator | The active category list is longer than a Jev `choice` accepts (255). | Retire categories that are no longer used with `ms category retire`. |
| `CATEGORY_UNKNOWN` | 3 | operator | `ms category retire` or a manual `ms tx tag` named a category the catalog does not hold (never created, a typo, or retired). | Use a name `ms category list` shows as active. A genuinely new category comes from `ms category propose` (an operator accepts it) or an operator's `ms category add`. |
| `CLIENT_EXISTS` | 3 | operator | Client exists. | The slug is already registered; change it with `ms client set <slug> ...` (see `ms client show <slug>`). |
| `CLIENT_INVALID` | 3 | you | Client invalid. | Give legal name, billing contact and clause as non-blank text. |
| `CLIENT_SET_EMPTY` | 3 | you | Client set empty. | Pass at least one of --legal-name, --billing-contact, --pass-through-markup, --contract-clause. |
| `CLIENT_SLUG_INVALID` | 3 | you | Client slug invalid. | Use a kebab-case slug: lowercase letters and digits joined by '-'. |
| `CLIENT_UNKNOWN` | 3 | operator | Client unknown. | Register the client first with `ms client register --slug ...`, or check `ms client list` for the exact slug. |
| `CONTRACT_CLAUSE_REQUIRED` | 3 | operator | A client would forbid markup with no contract clause of its own to cite (Story 6.1, D19): the guard never falls back to another client's agreement. | Name the clause of this client's signed contract that forbids markup on pass-through cost, e.g. --contract-clause "Master Agreement §3.4"; every guard refusal cites it. |
| `CONTRACT_REF_REQUIRED` | 3 | operator | A `service_fee` or `retainer` for a client that forbids markup names no contract (MILK-17, Story 7.3); or inference would be sold at the gateway list in a period the client forbids markup with no signed instrument behind it (Story 7.5). | Add --contract-ref "<signed instrument, section, date>" (for example "Maintenance Agreement s.4, signed 2026-12-01"). | `EVIDENCE_FILE_UNREADABLE` | 3 | you | Evidence file unreadable. | Pass a readable regular file of at most 20 MiB as --evidence-file. |
| `EVIDENCE_REQUIRED` | 3 | you | Evidence required. | Attach the source with --evidence-file PATH (an invoice or screenshot) or quote it with --excerpt "...". Never invent evidence; ask the operator for a real source if none exists. |
| `FARM_ACTOR_UNKNOWN` | 3 | operator | The signed `requested_by` is not an active invoicer on the ledger. Nothing is written. | An operator adds the person with `ms farm invoicer add --email ... --client ... --plan-all --reason ...`; the portal's own allow-list cannot widen this one. |

| `FARM_COMMAND_EXPIRED` | 3 | operator | The bridge accepted the command more than five minutes from its `issued_at`. | Ask again from the Farm; a command is only good for five minutes. |
| `FARM_COMMAND_INVALID` | 3 | operator | A Farm command is not the shape `docs/farm-commands.md` defines, or its `command_id` does not derive from its session and request ids. Nothing is written to the ledger. | The portal's server function builds the request; a malformed one is a bug there or a forgery. Ask the operator to look at the bridge's archive for this command_id. |
| `FARM_COMMAND_NOT_ALLOWED` | 3 | operator | The Farm asked for a command, a subject, a mode or an argument the allow-list does not hold (`farm/schema/ms-commands-v1.json`, Story 10.2). Nothing is written to the ledger. | The Farm may send only the allow-listed commands, on their registered Bloodbank subjects, with their listed arguments. Adding one is an allow-list change an operator makes in Milkshake (and its subject in Bloodbank), never a retry. |
| `FARM_COMMAND_NOT_GRANTED` | 3 | operator | The sender's effective grant does not list the command (Story 10.3). Recorded as refused; nothing about the client's data was looked at. | An operator grants the command for this client with `ms farm invoicer add --email ... --client ... --grant "NAME=plan"`; the portal cannot widen a grant. |
| `FARM_COMMAND_STALE` | 3 | operator | An apply was consumed more than 15 minutes after it was signed. | Ask again from the Farm: an apply is only good for fifteen minutes. |
| `FARM_GENERATED_AT_FUTURE` | 3 | you | `generated_at` is more than five minutes ahead of the clock (it would pin the account page to a snapshot no later push could replace). | Omit --generated-at to stamp the current time, or give an instant that is not in the future (RFC 3339 with a timezone). A file exported with a future stamp cannot be pushed: export it again. |
| `FARM_GRANT_CLIENT_REQUIRED` | 3 | operator | `ms farm invoicer add` without `--client`: every new grant is per client (Story 10.3). | Name the client the grant is for: `ms farm invoicer add --email ... --client SLUG --plan-all --reason ...`. The legacy all-clients form can no longer be added. |
| `FARM_GRANT_FORBIDDEN` | 3 | operator | An agent address may not hold `apply` on an operator-authority command (Story 10.3). | Grant that address `plan` only, or grant the apply to a person's own email. |

| `FARM_INVOICER_UNKNOWN` | 3 | operator | `ms farm invoicer revoke` named an email, client or legacy grant that is not active. | `ms farm invoicer list` shows the active grants. |
| `FARM_KEY_UNKNOWN` | 3 | operator | The command is signed with a key id Milkshake does not hold. Nothing is written. | Add the key id to MILKSHAKE_FARM_COMMAND_KEYS (the same 1Password item the bridge reads) and restart milkshake-farm-consumer. |
| `FARM_MODE_FORBIDDEN` | 3 | operator | The invoicer may only ask for a plan (the command's `apply` is not granted). | Run the plan from the Farm and apply as an operator at the CLI, or grant the command's apply with `ms farm invoicer add --client ... --grant "NAME=apply"`. |
| `FARM_PUSH_CONFLICT` | 3 | operator | The portal answered 409: it already holds a different payload for this `generated_at`. | Snapshots are immutable. Recording a push moves the ledger head, so rebuilding with the same --generated-at yields different bytes: push the exact earlier bytes with `ms farm push --file PATH` (from `ms farm export`), or use a new --generated-at. |
| `FARM_PUSH_FORBIDDEN` | 3 | operator | The portal answered 403: the token is bound to another client, or an edge rule blocked it. | Use the token bound to this client and project. A Cloudflare edge block (the request carries a named User-Agent already) must be cleared in the portal's WAF rules. |
| `FARM_PUSH_INVALID` | 3 | operator | The portal answered 400, 413 or 422: it will not accept this payload. | The portal's schema or hash check refused the snapshot. Check that the portal vendors the same milkshake-v1.schema.json (`scripts/gen_farm_schema.py`) and has not drifted; nothing was recorded. |
| `FARM_PUSH_REJECTED` | 3 | operator | Any other refusal: an unexpected 3xx/4xx, or a 2xx that is not `{success: true}`. | Nothing was recorded. Check the portal's logs; the push is idempotent. |
| `FARM_PUSH_UNAUTHORIZED` | 3 | operator | The portal answered 401: the bearer is missing, malformed or unknown. | The token is not (or no longer) in the portal's MILKSHAKE_SNAPSHOT_CREDENTIALS. Check the 1Password item behind MILKSHAKE_FARM_TOKEN and that the portal has its hash. |
| `FARM_PUSH_UNAVAILABLE` | 3 | operator | The portal could not be reached, or answered 429 or 5xx. A retry is safe. | Retry later. The ingress is idempotent: re-sending the same bytes (`ms farm push --file PATH --apply`) cannot create a second snapshot. |
| `FARM_RUN_OUTPUT_INVALID` | 3 | operator | The command a Farm request ran ended without the JSON result line (Story 10.3). | Read `ms ledger log` for events under the run actor to see whether it wrote anything, then tell an operator. |
| `FARM_RUN_PLAN_WROTE` | 3 | operator | A Farm *plan* appended ledger events under its run actor: a bug in the CLI or the allow-list (Story 10.3). The events stay and the Farm shows the record as `failed`. | Stop and tell an operator: a plan must write nothing. `ms ledger log` shows the events. |
| `FARM_RUN_TIMEOUT` | 3 | operator | The command a Farm request ran did not finish in five minutes and was killed (Story 10.3). Recorded as `failed`, or as `applied` with this code when it had already committed events. | Read `ms ledger log` for events under the run actor before asking again: a metered squeeze pays for its vendor calls every time it runs. |
| `FARM_RUN_USAGE` | 3 | operator | The CLI rejected the arguments the allow-list produced (exit 2): the allow-list and the command disagree, which is a bug (Story 10.3). Recorded as `failed`. | Report it to an operator: the committed ms-commands/v1 no longer matches the ms tree (`mise run farm:commands` regenerates it). |
| `FARM_SIGNATURE_INVALID` | 3 | operator | The HMAC does not match the canonical request. Nothing is written. | The key in the portal's MILKSHAKE_COMMAND_HMAC_KEY differs from the ledger side's, or the body was altered after signing. Nothing was done. |
| `FARM_SNAPSHOT_INVALID` | 3 | you | `--file` is not the canonical `milkshake/v1` JSON that `ms farm export` writes. | Push a file written by `ms farm export` and not edited since: the bytes must be the canonical JSON and `payload_sha256` must match them. Or omit --file to build a fresh snapshot. |
| `FARM_SNAPSHOT_TOO_LARGE` | 3 | you | The snapshot is over the portal's body limit (512 KB): the portal would answer 413. | Push fewer periods at a time (`--period YYYY-MM`, one month is well under 64 KB). Nothing was sent or recorded. |
| `FARM_TOKEN_INVALID` | 3 | operator | The token holds whitespace or non-ASCII characters, or is shorter than the portal's 32-character minimum, so it cannot be the minted bearer. Refused before any request. | Re-save the 1Password field as the bare minted token (at least 32 characters, no spaces or newline). |
| `FARM_TOKEN_MISSING` | 3 | operator | `--apply` needs the client's Farm bearer (`MILKSHAKE_FARM_<CLIENT>_API_TOKEN`, else the legacy `MILKSHAKE_FARM_TOKEN`) and neither is set. | Run through `mise run ms -- farm push ... --apply` so `op run` supplies the client's MILKSHAKE_FARM_<CLIENT>_API_TOKEN (or the legacy MILKSHAKE_FARM_TOKEN) from .env.vendors.op. A token is never a command-line argument. |
| `FARM_URL_INVALID` | 3 | operator | `MILKSHAKE_FARM_URL` is not a plain https origin (the bearer token would leak). | Set MILKSHAKE_FARM_URL to an https origin such as https://www.automaticai.io (no credentials, query or fragment), or unset it for the default. Plain http is allowed only for localhost. |

| `FETCH_FAILED` | 3 | you | `ms boi fetch --apply` reached the vendor's page but recorded nothing: no invoice for the period, a document it could not read, or several matching invoices. | `GUARD_MARKUP_FORBIDDEN` | 3 | operator | Guard markup forbidden. | Charge AAI's own work as a fee with `ms rule add service_fee --reason ...` (outside the guard), or, only if the contract changed, `ms client set <slug> --pass-through-markup allowed` (itself a ledger event). |
| `INVOICE_UNREADABLE` | 3 | you | A downloaded invoice document did not yield a total, an invoice number and a service period, so the fetcher refuses to guess. | Open the document, then record it by hand with `ms boi add --manual ... --evidence-file`. |

| `ISSUER_INVALID` | 3 | you | Issuer invalid. | Give non-blank text of at most 500 characters, up to 8 address lines, and net days as a whole number from 0 to 365. |
| `ISSUER_SET_EMPTY` | 3 | you | Issuer set empty. | Pass at least one of --legal-name, --address-line, --payment-instructions, --terms, --net-days. |

| `ITEM_UNKNOWN` | 3 | you | `ms item show` named a line that is not among the client's items for the period. | Name a row key, a vendor slug, or 8+ hex characters of a scope key or boi id exactly as `ms item list --client C --period YYYY-MM` prints them. |
| `JEV_REPLY_INVALID` | 3 | you | Jev answered, but not with the two answers that were asked. | The transaction stays untagged; re-run `ms tx categorize --apply` later or tag it by hand with the command `ms tx list --untagged` gives. |
| `JEV_TOKEN_INVALID` | 3 | you | The Jev token is empty, an unresolved `op://` reference, not a plain bearer string or the value of another credential Milkshake holds. | MILKSHAKE_JEV_TOKEN is the `milkshake` virtual key minted on jev.delo.sh (never the ingress master key, a TypeSafe provider key or another consumer's key). |
| `JEV_UNAVAILABLE` | 3 | you | Jev could not answer one request (unreachable, an error status, a timeout). Never fatal to a sync or a tag: the transaction stays untagged with its `ms tx tag` command. | Re-run `ms tx categorize --apply` later (answers already received are cached by content), or tag the transaction by hand with the command `ms tx list --untagged` gives. |
| `JEV_UNCONFIGURED` | 3 | you | `ms tx categorize --apply` has transactions to ask about and no Jev token (Story 9.4). | Run it through `mise run ms -- tx categorize --apply` so op run injects MILKSHAKE_JEV_TOKEN from .env.vendors.op (the `milkshake` LiteLLM virtual key). The plan needs no key; `ms tx tag` tags by hand. |
| `LEDGER_BLOB_MISMATCH` | 5 | stop | Ledger blob mismatch. | Do not edit the ledger by hand. Restore the latest verified backup (ms ledger backup --to PATH makes one) and re-run ms ledger verify. |
| `LEDGER_BLOB_ORPHAN` | 5 | stop | Ledger blob orphan. | Insert a blob in the same command transaction as the event that references it. |
| `LEDGER_BUSY` | 3 | you | Another writer held the ledger's write lock for longer than a writer waits (MILK-11). | Another ms command is writing the ledger (squeeze --apply holds the lock while it calls vendors). Nothing was written: wait for it to finish, then retry. |
| `LEDGER_CHAIN_BROKEN` | 5 | stop | Ledger chain broken. | Do not edit the ledger by hand. Restore the latest verified backup (ms ledger backup --to PATH makes one) and re-run ms ledger verify. |
| `LEDGER_COPY_MISMATCH` | 5 | stop | A migrated or exported ledger does not match its source: the head, the counts, the digests or the fold differ (Story 8.3). | Do not use the copy. The source is untouched. A failed migrate rolls the whole copy back (the target stays empty and migrate can be run again) and a failed export file is removed; if the source moved during the copy, stop every writer first. | `LEDGER_CORRUPT` | 5 | stop | The ledger file is not a readable sqlite database, or its schema version was reset. | Do not edit the ledger by hand. Restore the latest verified backup (ms ledger backup --to PATH makes one) and re-run ms ledger verify. |
